column1: # #1006 shared hand oracle: the predicate candidate decides the whole parse at the full-input entry.
# Grammar: scope("😀\r\n" X 'c') over "😀\r\nc"; X is predicate(shape), or for UBNF:... the rule
# `@predicate R ::= shape` referenced from the entry (both frontends lower `LA | 'z'` to a Choice and a
# single element to a one-element Chain; Java emits LazyChoice / LazyChain). The callback reads the text,
# so a wrong candidate flips acceptance: with oneOf:c the parse succeeds exactly when the candidate is "c",
# with its complement exactly when it is not. Same contract as classic.tsv for the consumed kind.
# Collectors (Opt, Rep = ZeroOrMore / repeat_java, Rec = recovery with sync ";") return their consumed
# collection (#1023): a MatchOnly child contributes nothing, and a host projection (proj = "Z" / proj0 = ""
# whose logical start is 0) is collected, so the predicate fails with predicate_source instead of reading
# the input at the cursor. Rows from Opt[MO] on are Java measured.
